evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|child}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċild}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kilþ}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*kelþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kelþaz||[[womb]]; [[fetus]]}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵelt-||[[womb]]}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gel-||to ball up, amass}}. Cognate with {{cog|da|kuld||[[brood]], [[litter]]}}, {{cog|sv|kull||[[brood]], [[litter]]}}, {{cog|is|kelta}}, {{m|is|kjalta||[[lap]]}}, {{cog|got|𐌺𐌹𐌻𐌸𐌴𐌹||[[womb]]}}, {{cog|sa|जर्त}}, {{m|sa|जर्तु||tr=jártu|[[vulva]]}}.

"fetus, infant, unborn or newly born person," from Proto-Germanic *kiltham (source also… See origin and meaning of child. from Proto-Germanic *kiltham (source also of Gothic kilþei "womb," inkilþo "pregnant;" Danish kuld "children of the same marriage;" Old Swedish kulder "litter;" Old English cildhama "womb," lit.
